{"ac_map":[{"parent_ac":"1) TestClaudeTuiSessionPoolReusesAndClears asserts /clear is issued between consecutive turns sharing a working directory and that the underlying PTY session is reused (same pid).","coverage":"Session-pool child AC #1 (TestClaudeTuiSessionPoolReusesAndClears) — covers /clear-between-turns and same-pid reuse via the new package-scope pool and Session.Pid() accessor."},{"parent_ac":"2) TestClaudeTuiOrphanReaper asserts that on harness shutdown any leftover PTY child processes are reaped within a bounded timeout.","coverage":"Orphan-reaper child AC #1 (TestClaudeTuiOrphanReaper) — covers bounded-timeout SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL reaping of live PTY children on Harness.Shutdown."},{"parent_ac":"3) go test ./... -count=1 is green.","coverage":"Both children AC #2 — each child carries the `go test ./... -count=1` gate."},{"parent_ac":"4) lefthook run pre-commit is green.","coverage":"Both children AC #3 — each child carries the `lefthook run pre-commit` gate."}],"child_ids":["fizeau-fe0b715f","fizeau-04d91f3b"],"rationale":"The parent carries exactly two independent functional concerns that map to distinct ADR-013 §3 decision items: pooled session reuse with /clear-between-turns (item 4) and the orphan reaper (item 6). They touch different code paths (Execute/runTurn + a package-scope pool + a Session.Pid() accessor vs. a new Harness.Shutdown reaper driving Session.Close/Kill/Wait) and have separate, independently verifiable Test* symbols, so a 2-way split is the natural minimal decomposition; a 3+ way split would only fragment the pool logic artificially. The reaper child depends on the pool child because Shutdown reaps the pool's tracked sessions. Every parent non-scope item, the CONTRACT-004 and internal/pty/ governing references, the child #1 / sibling child A dependency IDs, and both verification gates are preserved verbatim in each child, with each child additionally non-scoping the other's surface."}
